newsitem.title: INDIA: Grenades explode outside Kashmir polling stations.
newsitem.headline: Grenades explode outside Kashmir polling stations.

text.p: Suspected separatist militants hurled grenades outside two polling stations in southern Kashmir on Monday, injuring three paramilitary troopers, witnesses said.

One grenade exploded near a polling station in Dialgam village as a group of journalists arrived to observe the second phase of elections in Jammu and Kashmir state which have been marked by anti-government protests.

Dialgam resident Ghulam Mohammad told Reuters there had been at least two other grenade attacks since Sunday evening in nearby Anantnag town, located 50 km (30 miles) south of the state's summer capital Srinagar.

The state, torn by a six-year separatist revolt, is holding its first assembly elections since 1987. The first stage of the four-phase polls was held on September 7, and voters were set to cast ballots in the second phase on Monday in parts of the Kashmir and Jammu regions of the state.

At least 20 people, most of them political activists, have been killed during campaigning. Several candidates including Farooq Abdullah, head of the state's largest party, the National Conference, have escaped attacks.

Separatist groups called a state-wide strike on Monday to protest against the polls. Polling stations in Anantnag and neighbouring Pulwana town were largely deserted after they opened at 7 a.m. (0130 GMT), residents said.
